_README: Golden traces for PCAM ↔ CTM+ KVCachePolicy conformance tests.
Each trace is INPUT ONLY — the reference implementation at
Tests replay the trace on both sides and assert equality at every step.
This file is intentionally human-readable so reviewers can see exactly
what behaviors the conformance suite exercises without running Python.
Source of truth for scoring model: docs/design/ADR-0001-CTM-KV-SCORING-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.md

single_key_saturation.description: Repeatedly increment one key. Estimate must rise 1..15 then saturate.
single_key_saturation.notes: After step 15 the counter is pinned at 15 (4-bit saturation). Steps 16+ must return 15.

distinct_keys_light_load.description: Many distinct keys, one touch each. Load factor << 1 so collisions are rare.
distinct_keys_light_load.notes: Key 9999 was never inserted. Its estimate must be 0. Inserted keys must be >= 1 (collisions may bump estimate higher, but never below true count).

halving_threshold.description: Push size past reset_threshold to force a halve.
halving_threshold.notes: The halve fires inside increment() when size >= reset_threshold, BEFORE the current key's counter is bumped. After halving, counters are right-shifted by 1 and size is halved. Every previously-saturated key must now estimate <= 7, and size must be 80.

post_halving_order_preservation.description: Keys with very different pre-halve counts must retain rough ordering after halving.
post_halving_order_preservation.setup: increment key 0 eight times, key 1 four times, key 2 two times, key 3 one time
post_halving_order_preservation.then: increment key 99 repeatedly until size crosses reset_threshold = 640
post_halving_order_preservation.notes: After one halving, estimates should be approximately 4, 2, 1, 0. Strict ordering breaks at the boundary (1>>1 = 0, 0>>1 = 0) but 0 >= 1 >= 2 >= 3 in raw count ordering must still hold at the estimate level.

hash_determinism.description: Two sketches of the same capacity must map identical keys to identical rows.
hash_determinism.notes: Structural check: for every key, the four hashed indices must match across any two FrequencySketch instances with the same capacity. This is what lets RTL's fixed seed constants be trusted.

sink_pinning.description: Sink positions (0..3) must never appear in victim sets, ever.
sink_pinning.assert: block_id 0 is NOT in the victim set (it is pinned via sink).

filler_fast_path.description: When enough all-filler blocks exist to satisfy the request, the fast path runs instead of sampled scoring.
filler_fast_path.attention_events: All blocks receive attention_sum = 0.005 (below entity threshold).
assert: filler_evictions counter in stats increases by 4.

entity_bonus_protection.description: High-attention non-sink blocks survive under eviction pressure.
entity_bonus_protection.assert: Blocks 0, 1, 2 must NOT be in the victim set. The +0.5 entity bonus should push their scores above any filler.

prefill_vs_decode_weight_shift.description: Same trace, different phase — different victim ordering must result.
prefill_vs_decode_weight_shift.attention_pattern: Gradient: block 0 gets 0.30, block 1 gets 0.28, ..., block 15 gets 0.0.
assert: Under PREFILL (attention weight 0.35), blocks 12-15 are evicted first.
Under DECODE (attention weight 0.30, recency 0.30), the recency component matters more — order may differ.
Critical: both sides must produce the SAME ordering under the SAME phase. Phase-sensitivity is the test.

sampled_path_determinism.description: When the filler set is smaller than the request, the sampled path runs. Same RNG seed must yield the same 48-candidate sample on both sides.
sampled_path_determinism.trace: 200 admissions, mixed sink/filler/entity, evict 32 at a time for 10 rounds.
sampled_path_determinism.assert: Victim sets match block-for-block across all 10 rounds. Any mismatch is a sampling-path divergence — check that PCAM and reference share the same random.Random(42) instance semantics.
